This privacy policy describes who we are, what information we collect from you, how we process your information, who we share it with, and your rights under data protection laws.
To make it easier for you to navigate this privacy policy, we have put certain words and phrases in bold . You can click on them to see a definition of the word or phrase.

Technical identifiers
To provide tailored content to you and to create content interest profiles based on your inferred interests.
We use AI and machine learning to rank, order and recommend the tailored content you see across our consumer services — for example, in Yahoo News, Sports and Finance.

For example, if you frequently read articles on our consumer services about sports or financial markets, we will create profiles that identify you as a ‘sports enthusiast’ or ‘financial news consumer’. When you visit our consumer services in the future, you will see more articles about those interests. Similarly, if you add a company’s stock symbol to your Yahoo stock portfolio, we will show you more news articles about that company.

If you withhold or withdraw your consent for us to use your personal information to provide tailored content to you, we will still show you content, but it will not be based on your inferred interests. Also, we will not use cookies and similar technologies to measure how you interact with the content we show you.

This includes, where you have consented, using your information to develop, fine-tune and improve the AI and machine-learning models that power features of our consumer services.
We do this by:

tracking how users navigate (move through) our services, analysing user interactions, studying the performance of key user flows (such as our checkout flow) to identify areas for optimisation which improves the usability of our sites and apps.

understanding user behavior to identify common behavioral patterns such as the most-visited pages and assessing how the changes we make to our sites and apps impact how users engage with our products and services. This helps us improve our products and services and anticipate user needs to enhance the overall user engagement on our consumer services.

To prevent and detect fraudulent, abusive, harmful or unlawful activity and to protect your account and our systems.
We use your IP address to protect our services from fraud and other harmful technologies and activities.

We also use AI and machine learning to moderate content and to maintain the quality and safety of our consumer services — including to detect, filter, remove or restrict harmful, abusive, misleading or low-quality content.

We also analyse your email information for viruses and other malware that would harm the performance or security of our email services and network, as well as to detect, prevent and protect against fraudulent, abusive, harmful or unlawful behaviour. For example, we use email information for performance monitoring, security analysis, failure and outage detection and repair, troubleshooting and debugging, capacity planning and forecasting, traffic optimisation and load balancing, and to maintain the integrity of our systems and services.

For example, we keep the content of your email account for as long as your account is active. To keep your account active you must log in at least once every 12 months. If your account becomes inactive, your mailbox will be automatically deleted and cannot be restored. If your account continues to be inactive for a further six months, making it inactive for a total of 18 months, your account will be automatically scheduled for deactivation and deletion by our systems. We will tell you using your alternative communications channel (if you have set one up) before this happens. For more information on our account deletion practices, please see information on Inactive mailboxes in Yahoo Mail or Reasons Yahoo deactivates or deletes an account

We keep the content of your mailbox for as long as your mailbox is active. To keep your mailbox active, you must sign in to Yahoo Mail and actually access your mailbox — for example, open and read your email — at least once every 12 months. Signing in to your Yahoo account alone is not enough, and other activity that does not involve you accessing your mailbox (such as simply continuing to receive emails) does not count.

If your mailbox becomes inactive because you have not accessed it for 12 months, it will be automatically deleted and the contents cannot be restored. Before this happens, we will give you advance notice by email, sent to the alternative email address associated with your account (if there is one setup on the account). We do not send these notifications by text message (SMS), so if you have not added an alternative email address, we recommend you do so as soon as possible to make sure you receive them.

Separately, your Yahoo account becomes inactive if you do not sign in to it for 24 months, after which it will be automatically scheduled for deactivation and deletion by our systems. Once an account is deleted it cannot be restored and is permanently blocked for re-use by anyone. For more information, please see Inactive mailboxes in Yahoo Mail or Reasons Yahoo deactivates or deletes an account .
